structure.subject: chunk types "tEXt", "zTXt", "iTXt", "tIME", "eXIf"
structure.detail: these may appear anywhere between IHDR and IEND, including after the IDAT run
structure.description: PNG 1.2 places no ordering constraint on the text and time chunks beyond the IHDR-first, IEND-last rule; placing some of them after IDAT reaches libpng's post-image chunk handling, which the pre-image position never does.
structure.output_budget: covered by the text-chunk budget above
structure.generation_note: scatter these through both the pre-IDAT and post-IDAT regions rather than clustering them in one place

structure.subject: chunk types "iCCP" and "sRGB"
structure.detail: a file should contain at most one of the two
structure.description: They give contradictory colour-space definitions; PNG 1.2 says they should not both be present.

structure.subject: chunk type "acTL"
structure.detail: acTL must appear before the first IDAT chunk, and at most once
structure.description: APNG 1.0 requires the animation control chunk to precede the image data; an acTL after IDAT makes the decoder treat the file as a still PNG.

structure.subject: chunk type "acTL"
structure.detail: an acTL chunk requires at least one fcTL chunk, and every fdAT chunk requires a preceding fcTL
structure.description: The animation control chunk declares frames that the frame control and frame data chunks must actually supply.

structure.subject: chunk types "fcTL" and "fdAT"
structure.detail: each frame is one fcTL followed by the fdAT chunks carrying that frame's data; the fcTL/fdAT sequence numbers form one gapless run starting at 0, and fdAT chunks belonging to one frame must be consecutive
structure.description: APNG 1.0 makes the shared sequence numbering the ordering mechanism, and a decoder abandons the animation at the first out-of-order number.
structure.output_budget: 262144 bytes (256 KiB) of fdAT data summed across every fdAT chunk in the file. The generator keeps a running total across all frames and stops emitting further frames once it is reached; the number of frames and each frame's dimensions stay free and are never reduced to fit the budget -- the budget simply ends the frame sequence.
structure.generation_note: emit as a repeated group -- one fcTL chunk, then one or more fdAT chunks built from that fcTL's dimensions -- after the IDAT run, incrementing one shared sequence counter at every fcTL and every fdAT, and stopping when the running total reaches the budget

structure.subject: sPLT palette names
structure.detail: the paletteName of each sPLT chunk must be unique within the file
structure.description: PNG 1.2 clause 4.2.8 forbids two suggested palettes with the same name.
structure.output_budget: covered by the pre-IDAT ancillary budget; uniqueness adds no bytes
structure.generation_note: append a counter to the generated name when more than one sPLT chunk is emitted

structure.subject: PNG_CHUNK
structure.detail: the chunk sequence repeats until end of file, with IHDR as the first element and IEND as the last; any number of chunks may appear between them
structure.description: The main loop at lines 376-379 reads chunks until FEof(), so the chunk count is the file's principal repeating dimension.
structure.output_budget: 1048576 bytes (1 MiB) for the whole chunk sequence, signature included, tracked as a running total the generator checks before starting each new chunk. When the total is reached the generator stops opening new chunks and emits the IEND tail. The individual budgets above (768 KiB IDAT, 256 KiB fdAT, 128 KiB text, 16 KiB sPLT and the small fixed groups) are sub-allocations of this figure and are each tracked the same way. A megabyte is enough to hold a genuinely large image, a multi-frame animation and a full set of ancillary chunks while keeping generation and decoding fast across a large corpus. No field's value is ever narrowed to achieve this.
structure.generation_note: emit as a fixed head (signature and IHDR), then a repeated array of chunks drawn from the legal types for the current position and bounded by the running output_budget, then a fixed tail (IEND)

structure.subject: any chunk before IHDR or after IEND
structure.detail: nothing may sit between the signature and IHDR, and nothing may follow IEND
structure.description: Both are structural rules a decoder enforces immediately; the template's own closing checks at lines 381-387 test the same two positions.

diversity_axes.why: Width sets the row stride, the sub-byte packing arithmetic, the seven Adam7 pass widths and the size of every row buffer libpng allocates; it is the field a size-conscious author is most tempted to pin, and pinning it is exactly what cost 1.7 coverage points on GIF.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: widths of 1-7 with a bit depth below 8 leave a partially filled final byte and drive the row-mask and png_do_unpack paths; byte-aligned widths take the fast copy path; widths above libpng's default user limit of 1000000 reach png_set_user_limits and the 'width exceeds user limit' rejection; odd versus even widths change which Adam7 passes are non-empty.

diversity_axes.why: Height sets how many filtered scanlines the IDAT stream carries and therefore how many times the filter reconstruction and row-callback code runs; narrowing it makes every image the same shape.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: height 1 means there is no previous row, so the Up, Average and Paeth filters take their first-row special cases; heights below 8 leave some Adam7 passes empty, a distinct branch in the pass loop; large heights reach the user-limit and row-allocation checks.

diversity_axes.why: The bit depth decides whether samples are sub-byte, byte-aligned or 16-bit, which selects three different unpacking and transform pipelines; for a Tier B axis staying unconstrained means emitting all five legal values, not favouring 8.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: depths 1, 2 and 4 are the only way into png_do_unpack, png_do_expand and the sub-byte row-mask arithmetic; depth 8 takes the direct path; depth 16 reaches png_do_scale_16_to_8, png_do_swap and the 16-bit-specific filter arithmetic.

diversity_axes.why: The colour type sets the channel count and decides which of bKGD, sBIT, tRNS, hIST and PLTE are legal, present or differently shaped, so it fans out into most of the ancillary chunk handlers; staying unconstrained means emitting all five legal values.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: type 3 is the only route into the palette expansion, the palette-index checks and hIST; type 0 and 4 reach the greyscale-to-RGB expansion; type 2 and 6 reach the truecolour path; types 4 and 6 reach the alpha compositing and premultiply code that the others never touch.

diversity_axes.why: Adam7 versus no interlace is the single largest fork in libpng's row handling; emitting only one of the two legal values throws away the other half of that code outright.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: method 1 is the sole entry into png_do_read_interlace, the pass offset and increment tables, the seven-pass outer loop and the sparse row-copy code; method 0 is the sole entry into the straight sequential row path.

diversity_axes.why: The chunk type is what decides which decoder function runs at all; every registered type left out of the generated mix is a whole handler that never executes, and unregistered types are the only route into the unknown-chunk path.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: each registered type maps to its own png_handle_* function; critical versus ancillary changes the CRC-failure behaviour from fatal to skip; an unknown type reaches png_handle_unknown, png_crc_finish and the chunk-skipping loop.

diversity_axes.why: The palette entry count is a count that feeds an allocation and a loop bound, so it is exactly the sort of field a careful reader is tempted to fix at 256; but it also sets the legal spans of tRNS, hIST and the bKGD index, and fixing it collapses all of those at once.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: small palettes with a larger bit depth reach the index-out-of-range checks; a palette smaller than 2^bits reaches png_check_palette's short-palette handling; a 256-entry palette takes the full-table path; the count also decides whether a tRNS or hIST chunk of a given length is accepted.

diversity_axes.why: The sample depth selects the six-byte or ten-byte sPLT entry layout and therefore two different unpacking loops; the entry array must be derived from it, not the depth chosen to suit a fixed blob.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: depth 8 takes the single-byte sample read path; depth 16 takes the big-endian uint16 unpacking path and a different entry-size multiplication in the length check.

diversity_axes.why: The flag decides whether the iTXt text goes through inflate or is copied verbatim; emitting only one value deletes one of the two paths entirely, and the payload must be built from the flag rather than the flag pinned to suit a fixed payload.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: flag 1 is the only route into png_decompress_chunk, the output-buffer growth loop and the decompression error handling for iTXt; flag 0 is the only route into the direct UTF-8 copy.

diversity_axes.why: The frame width sets the frame's row stride and the width of the composited region; it is the APNG equivalent of the GIF dimension that was wrongly shrunk, and the fdAT payload must be computed from it.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: a frame narrower than the canvas reaches the partial-row blend and clip code; a full-width frame takes the whole-row path; widths that interact with x_offset at the canvas edge reach the bounds rejection.

diversity_axes.why: The frame height sets how many scanlines the frame's zlib stream must carry and how many rows the compositor walks; the payload derives from it and it is never reduced to fit a payload.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: a frame shorter than the canvas reaches the partial-canvas update and the dispose-region restore; a full-height frame takes the whole-canvas path.

diversity_axes.why: The horizontal placement selects the clipping and offset arithmetic in the compositor; pinning it to 0 leaves every frame at the origin and deletes that arithmetic.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: a non-zero offset reaches the column-offset addressing in the blend loop and, combined with width, the canvas-overflow rejection; zero takes the aligned fast path.

diversity_axes.why: The vertical placement selects which row range the compositor writes and restores; pinning it removes the row-offset arithmetic.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: a non-zero offset reaches the row-offset addressing and the partial dispose-region restore; zero takes the aligned path.

diversity_axes.why: The frame count drives the animation loop bound and is the obvious field to pin small; but it also decides how many fcTL/fdAT groups exist, which is the repetition the animation code is built around.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: a single frame skips the dispose and restore machinery entirely; two or more frames reach the previous-frame snapshot, the dispose operations and the inter-frame blending; a count that disagrees with the actual fcTL count reaches the frame-count validation branch.

diversity_axes.why: Text length and content are free, and varying them is what drives the text-storage growth and the string-handling code; a fixed string would make every tEXt chunk identical.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: empty text, very long text and text containing high-bit Latin-1 bytes take different paths through png_set_text_2's allocation and the caller's text handling.

diversity_axes.why: Pixel density is unvalidated numeric data, and a size-conscious author would be tempted to fix it at 2835; zero and extreme values reach guard branches a fixed value never would.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: zero reaches the divide-by-zero guard in the aspect-ratio helpers; very large values reach the overflow checks in png_get_x_pixels_per_inch.
